title: Cross-stack pause-and-patch strategy for heterogeneous rollout regressions
creator: Claire Huang
description:
Purpose: Establish a pragmatic, platform-agnostic runbook for detecting, pausing, and patching model rollout regressions that may surface differently across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. The goal is to minimize customer impact and time-to-correct while preserving auditability and traceability for enterprise customers.

Scope: Incidents where a new model variant or config rollout causes measurable regressions (latency, token-error rate, hallucination frequency, output structure regressions) at canary or early production traffic. This covers: hosted API rollouts, reserved pools (Dedicated), and private VPC/on-prem deployments where we coordinate with Customer SRE/infra.

Success criteria:
- Mean time to containment (pause or fallback) <= 10 minutes after regression detection alert.
- Rollback or hotpatch applied and validated across affected tenants within 120 minutes for Hosted/Dedicated, and coordinated target of 8 hours for Private (customer-dependent).
- Customer comms initiated within 15 minutes for high-impact tenants.

Runbook (high level):
1) Detection & Triage:
   - On-call receives alert from canary SLO probe, quality regression monitors, or customer report.
   - Confirm scope (model id, variant, rollouts, affected regions/GPUs, tenant list). Use telemetry dashboards: per-route latency, token error rates, eval-run prompt-set regressions (links below).

2) Containment (Pause / Fallback):
   - Hosted: Trigger automated rollout pause and shift canary traffic to previous stable model variant via rollout controller. If automated pause fails, use manual route pinning in Console (PR/route override).
   - Dedicated: Quiesce affected GPU pools (prevent new model tasks) and attach per-tenant fallback routing to pre-rollout endpoint. Use reserved capacity controller to avoid disrupting other tenants.
   - Private: Escalate to customer SRE; apply route-level override or instruct customer operator with a signed minimal configuration to revert to previous model. Provide precise rollback artifact (model hash, config).

3) Rapid Mitigation (Patch-or-Rollback):
   - Preference order: 1) Fast rollback to last verified variant; 2) Minimal hotpatch (config/kernel flag) if root cause is config/optim; 3) Full model rebuild if necessary.
   - Draft a short remediation plan and announce in incident channel. Attach candidate PR(s) and QA checks.

4) Validation and Observability:
   - Run targeted canary set (sparse traffic) with golden prompts and compare scoring metrics. Validate latency and correctness thresholds.
   - Confirm metrics for affected tenants; run smoke tests for downstream features (function calling, streaming).

5) Customer comms and post-incident actions:
   - Notify affected customers with timeline, action taken, and mitigations. For Private deployments, include exact upgrade/reversion commands and audit artifacts.
   - Create follow-up tasks: root-cause analysis, regression test additions, model gating changes, and automation gaps.

Decision criteria matrix (quick):
- If regression produces increased safety violations or hallucinations -> immediate rollback.
- If regression is purely performance (latency) and traceable to kernel scheduling -> consider hotpatch first.
- If regression affects tenant-specific behavior -> prioritize tenant-aware rollback (route pinning) rather than full rollout stop.

Operational notes:
- Always capture model hash and rollout id in the incident ticket.
- For Dedicated pools, check quota/burst policies before applying route fallback to avoid capacity bleed.
- For Private, maintain signed rollback bundles in the private artifact store and verify customer signature checks.

Links to artifacts and references:
- Canary health dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/canary-health
- Regression eval harness: https://drive.google.com/regression-evals-runsets
- Patch PR template: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/REPLACEME
- Private rollback bundle (internal storage): https://drive.google.com/private-rollbacks

Notes on automation opportunities:
- Add automated route pin in Console that can apply tenant-scoped overrides within 2 clicks for P0 incidents.
- Improve canary triggers with multi-metric fusion (latency + output-quality score) to reduce false-positives.
- Build a verified rollback artifact registry that surfaces compatible previous variants and required kernel/quant flags.

Compliance and audit: Ensure all actions taken for Dedicated/Private are recorded in audit logs with actor and timestamp. For customer-facing incidents, collect consented evidence before sharing logs derived from tenant data.
